dedupe_keys.name: pnnl fragility functions resource report for electricity and water resilience valuation pnnl 33587

description: This PNNL report collects documented fragility functions, which relate hazard intensity to the probability of damage, for electricity and water infrastructure assets, with links to their original sources, to support valuation of resilience investments at federal installations. It covers assets such as generators, wind turbines, solar PV, switchyards, substations, power lines, hydropower systems and water distribution, grouped by hazard: earthquakes (including the CLIP lifelines fragility database, transformers and substation equipment), wind, hurricanes, ice loads, floods, tsunamis, volcanic activity, geomagnetic storms, heat, tornadoes and power outages. It was written by Wilfried Kabre and Mark Weimar at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory for the US Department of Energy and published in October 2022. The 76-page report is available as a free PDF from PNNL; as a US Government sponsored report it carries a standard disclaimer and no open licence. Caveats: it points to fragility curves in other publications, not providing a harmonised machine-readable library. It supports hazard exposure, cascading failure and resilience investment analysis of energy and water systems across many hazards; a related record is the GEM empirical fragility and vulnerability compendium.
